vr.label: VR headset
vr.why: {t} supports VR. The Quest 3S is the cheapest way into PC VR over Air Link or a cable; the Quest 3 adds sharper pancake lenses.

hotas.label: Flight stick and throttle
hotas.why: A stick and throttle makes flying in {t} feel like a cockpit instead of a keyboard. The HOTAS One works on PC and Xbox.

wheel.label: Racing wheel
wheel.why: A force-feedback wheel and pedals give real throttle and brake control in {t}. The G29 is the best-value wheel; the G923 adds smoother TrueForce feedback.

fps_mouse.label: Low-latency mouse
fps_mouse.why: Fast aim in {t} needs a light mouse with a quick wireless link. The G305 is a cheap lag-free wireless pick; the Superlight 2 is what pros use.

comp_kb.label: Fast keyboard
comp_kb.why: Quick, consistent keys for movement in {t}. The Huntsman V3 Pro adds rapid-trigger switches that reset the moment you let go.

comp_monitor.label: High-refresh monitor
comp_monitor.why: Higher refresh means smoother motion and quicker reactions in {t}. Both are sharp 1440p screens at 165Hz or more for the price of a 1080p monitor.

comp_headset.label: Headset with a clear mic
comp_headset.why: Hear footsteps and give callouts in {t}. The BlackShark V2 X is a light budget headset with a mic teammates can hear; the Cloud III is a step up in comfort and sound.

chat_headset.label: Headset for co-op voice chat
chat_headset.why: {t} is better with friends on voice. The Cloud III has a clear detachable mic; the G733 goes wireless for long co-op nights.

mic.label: Microphone
mic.why: For crisp voice chat or streaming {t}, a desk mic beats any headset mic. The AM8 is a great USB starter; the QuadCast S is the creator favorite.

controller.label: Controller
controller.why: {t} plays great on a controller. The 8BitDo Ultimate 2C is a cheap, reliable PC pad; the Ultimate 2 adds drift-free Hall effect sticks and a charging dock.

sports_pad.label: Controller
sports_pad.why: Sports games like {t} are built around a controller. The Xbox pad works on PC with no setup; the DualSense Edge adds back buttons and swappable sticks.

big_monitor.label: Monitor for the best visuals
big_monitor.why: Show off {t} on a sharp 1440p screen. The SANSUI is the budget pick; the 32-inch curved Odyssey wraps the picture around you.

detail_monitor.label: Monitor with room for maps and menus
detail_monitor.why: 1440p gives {t} far more screen space for maps, menus and UI than 1080p.

strat_mouse.label: Mouse with extra buttons
strat_mouse.why: Bind hotkeys to side buttons and spend long sessions in {t} comfortably. The G502 is the classic; the Lightspeed version cuts the cord.

type_kb.label: Keyboard
type_kb.why: Lots of hotkeys and typing in {t}. A solid mechanical board makes long sessions easier on your hands.

immersive_headset.label: Headset for immersive sound
immersive_headset.why: Atmosphere is half of {t}. The Cloud III has rich spatial sound; the Arctis Nova 7 goes wireless with long battery life.

speakers.label: Speakers
speakers.why: Relaxed games like {t} sound great on desk speakers. The Pebble V3 is tiny and cheap; the Edifier G2000 fills the room.

ambience.label: Room lighting
ambience.why: Light bars that sync colors to the screen make the scary parts of {t} hit harder after dark.

gpu.label: Graphics card upgrade
gpu.why: {t} recommends a strong graphics card. The RTX 5060 is the value upgrade for 1080p with DLSS; the RX 7800 XT handles 1440p at high settings.

deck_storage.label: Steam Deck storage
deck_storage.why: {t} runs on Steam Deck. A fast microSD card adds room for it and the rest of your library.

chair.label: Chair for long sessions
chair.why: {t} is the kind of game you lose hours in. Back support matters.

mousepad.label: Mousepad
mousepad.why: A big, consistent surface for wide aim sweeps in {t}.
